claims.text: The formation and distribution of grain-boundary nanoclusters govern toughness retention or loss in single-phase CrMnFeCoNi alloys.
The grain-boundary nanoclusters are composed primarily of segregated Cr, Ni, and Mn.
Controlled annealing can suppress or redistribute the grain-boundary nanoclusters.
Suppressing or redistributing the nanoclusters enhances grain-boundary cohesion.
Enhanced grain-boundary cohesion improves fracture toughness.
Conventionally heat-treated CrMnFeCoNi contains naturally occurring grain-boundary nanoclusters.
Naturally occurring grain-boundary nanoclusters in the conventional material lead to its standard toughness level.
Annealing at 800–900 °C with varied dwell times modifies the kinetics of grain-boundary segregation.
The proposed annealing protocol reduces detrimental nanocluster density relative to conventional treatment.
Cr-, Ni-, and Mn-containing grain-boundary nanoclusters reduce intergranular cohesion.
Reduced intergranular cohesion lowers fracture toughness.
A more homogeneous nanocluster distribution improves grain-boundary cohesion.
Improved grain-boundary cohesion increases resistance to crack initiation and propagation under mechanical stress.
Optimized heat-treated samples will exhibit a statistically significant increase in fracture toughness relative to conventionally treated samples.
Optimized heat-treated samples will exhibit delayed crack initiation relative to conventionally treated samples.
If nanocluster density is not significantly altered, toughness retention will not improve.
The proposed relationship is expected to apply to single-phase CrMnFeCoNi processed within the specified annealing conditions.
The proposed relationship may not apply outside the specified processing range or to substantially different alloy compositions.
Failure of the optimized treatment to reduce nanocluster density would falsify the claim that nanoclustering governs toughness retention.
A significant reduction in nanocluster density without a corresponding toughness increase would falsify the proposed causal mechanism.
